title: Space Simulation by a Turing Machine
statement: Let $P$ be an extended word-RAM program, let $g$ map Boolean lists to Boolean lists, and let $c,F_0\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every Boolean input list $x$, there are a time bound $t$ and a Boolean value $v$ such that $P$, started with word width $c(\lfloor\log_2 |x|\rfloor+1)$ and no random bits, halts in fewer than $t$ steps, outputs $g(x)$, and touches at most $F_0$ memory addresses. Then there are a finite-state Turing machine $M$ and $a\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every Boolean input $x$, $M$ halts with output $g(x)$ and uses at most $a(\lfloor\log_2 |x|\rfloor+1)$ work-tape cells.
hypotheses_covered: A function $g$ from Boolean lists to Boolean lists
For every Boolean input $x$, there exist $t$ and $v$ satisfying the stated halting, output, time, and space conditions
